title: stream-resilience-param-gateway-tool-session-json-mode-negotiation
author: Jonah Park
description: Purpose: improve parity with OpenAI /v1/chat.completions while reducing stream instability and making tool/function calling resumable and machine-parseable. This PR adds a parameter gateway that unifies deprecated aliases and enforces sane defaults, implements a stream-resilience controller that sends heartbeat frames and enforces inflight token caps, and defines a lightweight TOOL_SESSION handshake and resumable partial-result protocol. Additionally, json_mode negotiation with a schema_hint header lets clients opt into structured outputs without surprising human-facing callers. The gateway maps legacy params (e.g., top_p vs nucleus) deterministically, coalesces stop strings and arrays, and preserves semantics when n>1 by explicit deterministic seeding. Streaming safeguards include heartbeat intervals, client ACK timeouts, and an adaptive inflight limiter that reduces token send rate if ACK latency rises. Tool session behavior: clients receive a TOOL_SESSION frame with session_id, expected_content_type, and resume_token; tool outputs are emitted as PARTIAL_RESULT frames and closed with TOOL_RESULT frames containing status and canonicalized output. JSON negotiation: json_mode values are off|loose|strict; strict enforces shaped output via a server-side shaper and rejects non-JSON tokens after a grace threshold. Rollout plan: feature gated, will rollout to canary and 10% of hosted traffic for 7 days before expanding. Backcompat: default paths maintain legacy framing; openai_compat flag enables the strict mapping and tool/session frames.
commits: feat(param): add v1 param gateway and alias normalization
feat(stream): implement heartbeat frames and inflight limiter
feat(tool): TOOL_SESSION handshake and PARTIAL_RESULT/TOOL_RESULT frames
feat(output): json_mode negotiation and server-side shaper (loose/strict)
test: end-to-end toolcall streaming with resume scenarios
docs: add migration guide and compatibility table
review_thread: Aisha Rahman (reviewer): How will strict json_mode affect existing customers who rely on free-form text?

Jonah Park (author): strict is opt-in and gated by json_mode header or tenant flag. For canary we also provide a per-tenant toggle and a graceful fallback that emits a LAST_TRACE token and switches to loose mode if shaping fails repeatedly.
Sergei Petrov (reviewer): The inflight limiter could interact poorly with our autoscaler; did you run synthetic burst tests?

Jonah Park (author): yes, we ran burst tests against the Dedicated canary pool and observed <5% additional tail latency. The limiter exposes tuning knobs and emits metrics stream.inflight_limit_ratio and stream.ack_latency for operator tuning.
Nora Alvarez (reviewer): Tool session resume semantics look solid. Request: include resume_token rotation and TTL to avoid stale resumes.
Jonah Park (author): added resume_token_ttl (default 15m) and rotation on TOOL_RESULT success; documented the TTL and added tests to ensure stale tokens are rejected.
Aisha Rahman (reviewer): CI had one flaky e2e run; re-ran and green. Approving pending release note.
release_notes: Added v1 chat compatibility layer: parameter gateway for legacy aliasing, streaming resilience with heartbeat and inflight limiting, TOOL_SESSION handshake and resumable partial tool outputs, and json_mode negotiation for structured responses. Feature is opt-in and rolled out gradually.
